experiment: E06b: route decisions on 20 hand-labeled scenarios
question: Does a cheaper model pick the right route for a request (none, default or advisor) as accurately as the baseline?
setup: 20 hand-labeled routing scenarios, 2 runs per model, strict parsing of the route from each answer, accuracy against the hand labels. Harder than E06a: the labels separate trivial requests (none) from ones that need the default model or the advisor.
finding: gpt-6-luna averaged 0.675 accuracy and deepseek-v4-flash 0.650, a one-item difference within run-to-run noise. Of the 27 misses across the 4 runs, 19 are on the same five items (1, 2, 6, 10, 12: cron debug and patch, inbox summary, tweet draft, typo fix, CSV conversion) where the label is 'none' and the models said 'default'; 7 are on two advisor/default boundary items (15, 20) and 1 is on item 18. The ceiling here is label quality, not model quality. luna was also cheaper in practice ($0.000124 vs $0.000852 per 20-scenario pass) because its input was prompt-cached.
limitations: one labeler; the 'none' definition is ambiguous
luna's billed input (3-6 tokens per run) reflects caching, not prompt size
notes: Models were called through an OpenAI-compatible router; names and prices are as recorded at run time.
